athlete.name: Mahleea Werline
athlete.bio: A relentless competitor with a flair for artistry, this gymnast captivates audiences on Vault, Bars, and Beam. Known for her grace and precision, she embodies both strength and elegance in every routine.

caption:
And sometimes I just think…how proud she must be. After everything she went through, to have successfully made it through all of her long suffering. How happy she must be knowing I finally made it. How satisfying it must feel to have her efforts pay off in success. To know that in everything and in anything, she never gave up. So as I continue through this beautifully layed out journey He’s prepared for me, I guess I’ve realized that after trying for so long, I’ve finally achieved the ability to be joyful and to have happiness wherever my feet may be. It’s not that I don’t have sadness, or pain, or even that I’m completely content with where I’m at. It’s that after everything I’ve been through and everything everyone has thrown at me, I’ve more than tested the “theory”. You can’t stop me, as long as I have Him. And for what must be the first time, everything that little girl pictured in her head, and even now, with all the dreams and goals I have that people laughed at or made sure to comment, saying how impossible it was… well I guess impossible is just a word for him and I. A word that sets my soul on fire, a word that screams “You can do it”!

#god #gymnastics #her #love #soulonfire

athlete.name: Landon Helms
athlete.bio: A fierce competitor with a passion for flight, this versatile athlete thrives in the air and on the track, blending agility and strategy. Always pushing boundaries, he inspires teammates with relentless determination.

caption:
Best training week of my life!!!

This week was by far my best training week in my entire life. What’s not included in here is our lactic workout (also killer), our speed endurance workout, and our endurance workout. 

Monday was hurdles and we went through a full flight of hurdles for the first time and we were just moving. We had cued something new and it really helped

Tuesday was high jump and out lactic workout. I just knew going into it I was going to clear 6’4” since I had those two really close misses the week previous. I was so stoked to finally get it because I’ve been putting so much work into high jump recently. Then the lactic workout got me bad but I finished the last rep being the best one by far helping me know my body’s in a good spot right now. 

Wednesday was off and found a really good way to finally help with my super tight calves 😂

Thursday was shot and speed endurance. Finally figured out some cues last week for shot and really built upon them this week. Finally feeling an unwinding feeling and having a really long strike on the shot. 

Friday was vault and felt a little zapped from the sprint endurance but still had a really good session and even got over some bars. 

Then today was endurance day and felt I really improved my pain endurance 😂 We always have those conversations in our heads during a long run (1k and 1500) of keeping the pace steady and not really going out too hard. I felt I made really good progress embracing the pain and pushing myself when I started to hurt. Good mind over matter type deal
.
.
.

This past week I had a really good high jump session where we really figured some cues out.

If you don’t know, high jump has been one of those events that’s I’ve struggled with a bit in the past but we’ve been gaining some momentum all throughout last season. 

This session specifically was our first from full approach for the year and we almost jumped 2” over my current PR!! Coach only gave me 2 attempts at it but it’s crazy to see how big of a difference just one or two cues can make. 

So excited to keep building and reaching new heights.

caption:
Goodbye 2025

Thank you, I’m not going to lie you were somehow the best and worst year of my life all wrapped in one, but I’ve learned so much about myself and my endurance, my long suffering, my pain, my grief and sadness and weaknesses and strengths, happiness, hope, joy, and excitement. My ability to love, and to be loved. And as always my innate ability to believe in the impossible. I never give up, and that’s is more than a fact. I hate to admit it but this year God said “When the time is right, so the Lord will make it happen.” and so it was though the time wasn’t right, but this next year… well I have a great feeling everything is going to change for the best.
I would tell you the plan but it isn’t mine to give, and funny part is I don’t know either. Who knows where I’ll go or what I’ll do, but He did give me a hint, “I know the plans I have for you, they are plans for good and not for disaster, to give you a hope and a future.” I may not know the end, but I know the one who does, so let’s do this together shall we? Let yourself be excited because who really knows what comes next…❤️

Thank you God!

#god #jesus #goodbye2025 #happynewyearseve #happynewyears

caption:
Joe Hudson | Flying Into Euros 🇬🇧

Joe Hudson of Keighley & Craven delivered a huge performance at the European Cross Country Trials last weekend, taking 5th place in a stacked senior men’s field, powered by Mango BICARRB.
 🥭

After an agonising wait over the weekend, we were thrilled to see his selection for Team GB confirmed this week 🤝

Joe has put together a standout autumn and winter, showing serious consistency: one of the fastest legs at the National Road Relays, a big run at the English Cross Country Relays, and a superb performance in Cardiff where he finished as one of the top Europeans at the IAAF Label XC Meet 📈

He now heads to Lagoa, Portugal, to take on Europe’s best in the senior men’s race. 

With the form he’s shown, Joe has every chance of making a real impact on the biggest stage, and hopefully helping Team GB secure a medal 🏅

We’re incredibly proud to support him with a cheeky FLYCARB bundle and can’t wait to see him don the red, white and blue 🇬🇧

Let’s go Joe, see you in Portugal mate!

#FLYCARB #XC #crosscountry #lagoa2025 #TeamGB

From the very beginning God’s plan was to create a world, love every human & every creature in it, & give them an abundant life. Unfortunately sin created a problem & caused a separation between God & His creation.

And His name is Jesus ✝️

God so loved this world that He sent Jesus. Are you willing to go & tell the world about Him?

I feel so blessed to still be doing what I love and getting to represent a school, state, and community that I grew up with and love so much!! Getting to run track and call it ‘work’ is the best thing ever. Even more so when you have a coaching staff that feels like family and a family of your own to come along the journey with you #dadstrength 
.
As we’ve been getting ready for this season, it finally feels like the years have been compounding and we’re hitting some big breakthroughs. We haven’t done many technical sessions so far but the progress that we’ve made feels like we never took a step back. If anything, we took a major step forward even from the end of last season. I won’t be opening up my indoors until late January but it’s really exciting to see where we’re at about 2 months out.

“I don’t like to sit still,” McGuire said. “The energy I bring to athletics can be channeled for the age group I want to teach.”

A lifelong competitor and youth soccer player from a family of educators in Fullerton, California, McGuire chose Boise State because of its soccer program, which has a strong reputation with the Slammers FC club where she played. She confidently declared a major in elementary education inspired by her dad and aunt, who teach special education and first grade, respectively.

Boise State’s elementary education program provides hands-on experience for teacher candidates in area classrooms, building the foundation of experience McGuire will need to be a successful educator.

“Even though it’s tiring sometimes going straight from practice to fieldwork or volunteering with the team, I love it,” McGuire said.

athlete.bio: Hailing from a small town, this tenacious playmaker thrives on the field, combining sharp instincts with relentless determination. Known for his camaraderie and strategic mind, he elevates every game with passion and skill.

caption:
You don’t see this very often… a punter throwing a touchdown let alone an Aussie! 

Oscar Doyle might be the first Australian to ever throw a touchdown pass in college football 🇦🇺🏈

Here’s what actually happened: this was off a field goal attempt that broke down. When the snap, hold, or timing goes wrong, the unit has a play called “fire.” That means instead of panicking, the holder or kicker picks up the ball, and everyone goes into scramble mode — tight end or fullback leaks out, and you try to make something happen.

It’s not something you ever want to rely on, and it’s not really a play you want to practice too often… but you rep it just enough so that in a real game, instincts can take over.

That’s exactly what happened here. Oscar stayed calm, and delivered a perfect pass to the corner for a touchdown.

I once botched a hold myself at LSU and ended up throwing it into the endzone… let’s just say it didn’t have the same result as Oscar’s perfect touchdown pass.

Pretty wild moment… not many punters can say they’ve got a passing TD to their name. Get around him 👏

caption:
Yesterday early morning, my dad passed away. He was 53. After hearing the news from my sweet mother, Matt and I watched the sunrise and piercingly felt his presence. He fought so hard for us, and he was so sad to leave us, and the doctors and surgeons and nurses did everything they could, but his body was too sick. To Doctor Selzman his heart surgeon, to Doctor Rennert his brain surgeon, Doctor Florido his heart failure doctor, Pete his physical therapist, and so many more, we thank you for using your gifts and talents to help so many people and their families. To our community of friends and family, thank you for your kind messages and help, you lift us up and give us strength. We are constantly reminded of the world’s goodness because of you. We have been flooded with your love, and will be getting back to messages as soon as we can. Grateful for many of your loved ones that have passed on who welcomed our dad with open arms; we have felt them near. We love you so much dad, you are everything to us. We hope we can continue your legacy of tender gentleness, humble kindness, and quiet, meaningful love.

We hope to give you funeral updates soon ❤️‍🩹

The good news of Jesus Christ is simply this: 

He loves you.

caption:
Kicking off a new chapter: @coltonboomer_ is back to play and ready to take the field with @boisestatefootball. 

As our latest #ArthrexAthlete, Colton overcame ongoing ankle instability with the help of #Arthrex innovation and the InternalBrace™ ligament augmentation repair. Gideon J. Lewis, DPM, trusted the InternalBrace procedure to restore strength and stability to Colton’s ankle in his planting foot, allowing him to return to kicking at full strength with his new squad.

Stay tuned for Colton’s full story—coming soon—and learn about minimally invasive solutions for treating chronic ankle instability at AnkleSprain.com  🏈

#Innovation #CollegeFootball #InternalBrace #Sponsored

The InternalBrace surgical technique is intended only to augment the primary repair/reconstruction by expanding the area of tissue approximation during the healing period and is not intended as a replacement for the native ligament. The InternalBrace technique is for use during soft tissue-to-bone fixation procedures and is not cleared for bone-to-bone fixation.

caption:
NCAA ALL-AMERICAN 🇺🇸
.
There’s so many emotions from this weekend but I’m feeling so grateful for how it all went. 

Coming into this meet, I was ranked #19 in the country, and to end up placing 9th is such an amazing accomplishment in and of itself. It was super tight and tough all the way through and to run an almost 8 second personal best in the 1500 was the cherry on top. So grateful that it allowed me to have yet another overall personal best in the decathlon and to raise my #3 mark in Boise State history. 

I feel at peace with how the meet went. There’s things I’d fix and things I’d do differently, but I was out there having fun again and loving what I was doing. So glad to have spent it with my coach, wife, daughter, parents, and so many other amazing individuals. We’ll be back…

caption:
Eeeee 🧙🏻‍♀️🪄
I made it.. I graduated 🎓
There were moments when the weight of it all felt unbearable. Times when I thought I’d hit rock bottom, only to discover there was still further to fall. This journey tested me in ways I never expected, but it also shaped me. It taught me resilience, deepened my empathy, and made me stronger in mind and spirit ✨
To my Mum and Dad, thank you. Thank you for standing by me through every breakdown, every anxious call, and all the moments when my silence was louder than words and my tears said what I couldn’t. I know it wasn’t easy for you 🤍
I have regrets, a room full of them. I regret not recognising my worth sooner, not seeing my strengths clearly, and not achieving all I know I’m capable of. But Alhamdulillah, I’m grateful. Through every setback, I grew and I learned. BSU will always have a special place in my heart but now it's time to turn the page and start a new chapter 🧡💙
Cheers 🥂

caption:
Why a Rise Ball & Change-Up Combo is Deadly ⚡🎯

✨Hitters that know how to handle a rise ball or anything up in the zone, know that they have to get the bat head out and start their swing early. ⏩ That aggressive mindset is exactly what sets them up to chase a ball in the dirt.

🔥A well-thrown rise ball forces hitters to commit early, trying to catch it out front. Then—just when they think they’ve timed it up—comes the change-up in the dirt. Their weight is already forward, their hands are already committed, and all they can do is chase. 🥴💨

caption:
wow where do I start, it’s been a year without you daddy.

Life often presents us with challenges that test our strengths and resilience. For me, it’s been a year having to face my most feared challenge of them all. Growing up I was quick to learn about cancer due to my father being sick, but with that you’d think life could just be an up and down roller coaster. In my eyes it wasn’t, i learned so much from this sickness. I learned how special life was and how important it is to love your loved ones so loud. not only that, I was able to learn how to be one strong individual all from you daddy. 

Now for reality… Grief, a pool of water that can suck you in so quickly if you enable it. Some of us handle it with grace, we smile when one brings up the name, say thank you to condolences being passed. Some of us handle it messy. Smearing our makeup while trying to catch our breath, feeling as if we can fill an ocean with our tears before they stop coming. And a few of us stay frozen for awhile. Unable to quite process, still feeling pretty okay because it hasn’t hit us, some of us stay in a shell for awhile, until we slowly begin to thaw out. Some of us may stay in this state for months, years, and some may never quite thaw. We all have our own journey and mine just happens to be a mix. And that’s okay, grief is the true roller coaster and it’s quite the learning process with myself. Life hasn’t been the same without you daddy but I know you’re pain free while having the best seat in the house, can’t wait till I get to see you again daddy, I love you very much.

caption:
Dad, words can’t describe how painful these past few days have been without you. My heart is shattered. I feel like a piece of me left when you did. Though it’s going to be hard there is no doubt in my mind that I will get through this with the strength you taught me to have. I’m so thankful that you no longer have to feel pain and I’m more thankful that you finally get to be with our heavenly father who has been waiting a lifetime for you. The way you fought so hard not just for yourself but for mom, sis, and I inspired me in so many different ways. You went headfirst into the storm and never turned back which shows what kind of person you truly are and always have been. You are the definition of a warrior who has left a legacy behind for all to see and admire. You have impacted so many people’s lives while also being the greatest example for sis and I. You taught me many lessons about life and how I should go about living it as a follower of Christ. Thank you for all the countless laughs and joy you brought to our family. Your humor is unmatched and I will never forget all the precious memories we made together. I’m so incredibly blessed to be able to call you my dad and I’m thankful for the 19 years we got to spend with each other. Even though time with you on this earth is no more, I know in my heart that you will be walking with me through this life every step of the way until my time comes to be with you again. Our relationship is something I will cherish for the rest of my life. I owe you everything dad. 
Luv’n you, me❤️

“Today you will be with me in Paradise”(Luke 23:43).

caption:

3:159 - "Put your trust in Allah".

My time competing in the NCAA XC Championships has come to an end. At first, I was disappointed with how I executed the race, but then I remembered I've come a long way to where I am now. I'm glad I've been given another chance to love the sport after falling back for a long time. So, although I was physically ready, I didn't believe in myself to put myself out there. But I know it will come with time, patience, and love. 
Alhamdulillah, for having such a supportive network back home and for having faith & trust in Allah, the one who guides & protects. This is the path that was written for me, and I will always be grateful for what I have, remain hopeful through difficult times, and be content with whatever outcome 🙏🏼

Remember, since there's so much conflict in the world right now, people dream of having the basic necessities we have, so always be grateful and appreciative of what you have. Also, look after yourself and your mental health. Words, thoughts, and mindsets have such a big impact on one's overall health 🤍

#alhamdulillah #allahismyguide #begrateful #mentalhealthisimportant

caption:
Today on the podcast is Ezra Teeples.

Ezra Teeples is a rising senior and two-time Washington 4A state champion at Kamiakin High School. He won the cross-country state title last fall (15:32.9) and the 1600m state title this past spring (4:13.96). 

He holds PR's of: 800m (1:58.72), 1600m (4:13.33), Mile (4:17.31), 3200m (9:15.53).

We discuss Ezra's high-mileage and goals for his senior year, the importance of hard work and mental toughness, the influence of his family and teammates, and the increasing competitiveness of high school running. 

Ezra provides insights into his training, recovery routines, and experiences from last season's races, including the state meet and NXR. 

Tune in for an inspiring conversation about dedication, strategy, and personal growth in the sport of running.

I hope you enjoy this episode of The Sunday Shakeout!

#run #running #runners #highschool #crosscountry #xc #podcast

caption:
🥇South Australian Junior Girls Amateur🥇

🏆Junior Girls Invitational

What a great start to 2024 winning the South Australian Junior Amateur, my first national title!!

So proud to win this at my home club @kooyongagolfclub in my final year of junior tournaments. 

Over the 2 days I shot 77 (+3), 71 (-3) & 70 (-4) for a total of -4 to win by 2 shots.

Since I was the overnight leader with scores of 77 (+3) & 71 (-3) for even par, I also won the Kooyonga Summer Junior Girls Invitational.

So happy that all my hard work payed off and my golf finally came together which enabled me to win!! So happy that winning this tournament also gives me a world amateur golf ranking!!

Thanks to all my supporters it means a lot.
